compute.note: Parameters: 108 from the method string (high confidence); the circuit code builds 120 one-parameter gates (SU2_symmetrized_kagome18._get_dimerizarion_layers: range(2) x 60 pairs (13 patterns of 6,3,6,4,6,6,3,6,3,3,6,4,4)), which CONTRADICTS the stated 108: both kept, the stored value is the method string's. Iterations: 2000 = 1000 natural-gradient steps without symmetry projection, then 1000 continuing with the 24-element projector (n_iter default 1000; main.py is called twice and passes only lr). As published, Optimizer.optimize() ends with "return res.x" on the circuit object, which has no attribute x, so the first call exits with an AttributeError and "&&" would skip the symmetric run; the step counts are therefore what the code intends, not what it can be shown to have run, hence confidence low. Samples: none; the method string says exact gradients on a state vector. The code has no exact branch that main.py reaches: it draws binomial estimates with the default 2^36 shots (--log2samples default 36), which is exact to about 4e-6 relative. The script passes --lattice=kagome3x2, which main.py's argparse rejects (choices square4x4, triangle4x4, kagome2x3, square6x4): the script does not run as published. Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 2015a4d (2022-10-18, Nikita Astrakhantsev); the program was added to methods in 6887677 (2024-08-10) ("wip: added the VQE simulator"; next commit "VQE simulator: dusted-off version runs"), so it is a later reconstruction. The VarBench SM (arXiv:2302.04919 Sec. S3 D) describes the ansatz and the natural-gradient update but no step count.
